name: Taba Waku
description: First Cacique Má (516 CE). Started the calendar.

name: Bikabá Yabí
description: Catacomb builder. Early cacique.

name: Wirá Yabí
description: Cacique during great hurricane (1143 CE).

name: Waku Tabá
description: Reconstruction ruler (1162–1190 CE). Built inland capital post-hurricane.

name: Kanu Maku
description: Cacique. First tributaries established (~1300s).

name: Guani Buka
description: Cacique during population peak (~1400 CE). Trade expansion.

name: Warí Kuru
description: Cacique during cultural flowering.

name: Bika Kuru
description: Cacique during Kari Wirá (Tapuyic War). Commissioned sewn-plank war fleet.

name: Guani Waku
description: Cacique (912–938 CE). Attempted to assassinate Warí. Both died.

name: Yabí Tabá
description: Last pre-pestilence Cacique Má (reigned 1480–1536). Sent son to Lacashe 1523. Died during Great Pestilence.

name: Kari Buka
description: Captain ("Sea Opener"). Led Kari Yabí northern voyage (1502–1514).

name: Guled Badweyn
description: Burawi explorer. First contact with Guajicutea (Dec 5 1520).

name: Pere Vidal
description: Volisanian galleon captain. Brief stop at Guajicutea (April 1527).

name: Marcos Gabra
description: Father Marcos. Baraka Order missionary. Arrived 1523.

name: Dawit Wolde
description: Governor of Lacashe. Visited 1528. Recorded Yabí Tabá's 1523 son arrangement.

name: Yohannes Tadesse
description: Governor of Lacashe. Organized kingdom treaty (1536).

name: Boqor Petros I
description: Yabí Tabá's son. Baptized in Lacashe. First Boqor (1536–1554). Ruled from Tabakurí.

name: Boqor Petro II
description: Petros I's first son. Crowned and assassinated at coronation same day (1554).

name: Boqor Dawit I
description: Petros I's second son. Reigned 44 years (1554–1598). Volisania-backed.

name: Boqor Carlos I
description: Dawit I's son. First king with Sartan name. Reigned 1598–1609. Deposed during Sarta-Guajicutea War.

name: Buka Wariban
description: Bikabári of Waribá. Volisania conspirator. Seized Dabra during 1554 civil war.

name: Bishop Tekle Mariam
description: Bishop of New Burawa. Intervened 1543 to stop violence.

name: Governor Tewolde Berhe
description: Governor of Lacashe Province. Ordered cessation of hostilities 1543.

name: Diego Vela
description: First Sartan colonial governor (1609–1618). Oversaw establishment purge embargo first famine. Recalled 1618.

name: Alonso Mera
description: Second Sartan governor (1618–1630). Post-embargo stabilization trade resumption arrival cap.

name: Gabriel Soto
description: Third Sartan governor (1630–1640).

name: Hernán Vargas
description: Fourth Sartan governor (1640–1651).

name: Rodrigo Cifuentes
description: Fifth Sartan governor (1651–1663).

name: Mateo Salazar
description: Sixth Sartan governor (1663–1674).

name: Felipe Ortega
description: Seventh Sartan governor (1674–1691). Longest-serving. Overthrown and killed by peasant mob in Waribá (1691).

name: Waraku
description: Peasant ruler ("Turning Moon"). Seized power in Waribá during 1691 interregnum. Guaji name (warí+waku).

name: Captain Andrés Caldera
description: Sartan ship captain. Temporary administrator (1692–1705). Installed by Breisland-Mercia alliance.

name: Tomás Herrera
description: Civilian governor (1710–1723). Appointed after military rule under Caldera.

name: Don Vicente de la Vega
description: First Cónsul (1723–1727). Former Sartan nobleman. Republican leader. Convinced Sarta to cede colony.

name: Hernán Cifuentes
description: Cónsul (1739–1743). Cifuentes family.

name: Joaquín Delgado
description: Cónsul (1759–1763). Seized Astillero Real (1761).

name: Nicolás Vega
description: Cónsul (1763–1767). Formed Capuyaquiran and Abyalan League.

name: Diego Alvarado
description: Cónsul (1767–1771). Signed 1768 constitutional reform.

name: Lucas Cifuentes
description: Cónsul (1779–1783). Cifuentes family.

name: Carlos Mendoza
description: Cónsul (1783–1787). Church-limiting amendment (1784).

name: Felipe Rivera
description: Last Cónsul (1799–1801). Partial term.

name: Esteban Makurí
description: PD founder (late 1760s). Guaji native parish school-educated. Surname from makú + -rí.

name: Mateo Kurí
description: President (1804–1812). PD. First Guaji head of state. Exiled to Sarta 1813. Surname: kuri (stone) + -rí.

name: Ramón Cifuentes
description: NR exile leader. Former NR senator/landowner. Orchestrated 1812 coup with NC/Bayara. Cifuentes family. Installed as PUG civilian head. Fled during Virtuous Revolution.

name: Vittorio Calvi
description: Bayaran naval officer. NC military governor (1812–1820). Implemented race codes oversaw early Bloody Decade.

name: Marco Vendrell
description: Cerdanyan military officer. NC military governor (1820–1824). Oversaw late Bloody Decade and troop withdrawal.

name: Tomás Yukurí
description: Guaji former army officer. Guarda Revolutionary military commander. Highland terrain expert. Surname: yuku (mountain) + -rí.

name: Diego Nasarí
description: Bayani PD underground organiser. Guarda Revolutionary political commander. Surname from Arabic nasr (victory) + -í.

name: Javier Barirí
description: RG leader (1824–1828). First president of Second Republic (1829–1837). Served 2 terms. Retired July 1 1837. Died Aug 1 1837. Surname: bari (storm) + -rí = person of the storm.

name: Sebastián Biku
description: Proto-Symbolist painter. Central figure of movement. Early realist works documenting Bloody Decade then incorporated Bikumaku glyphs and three powers into canvases (late 1830s). Travelled to Sarta 1845 — bridge to Illpynia. Surname: bikú (carved year-mark) plain root.

name: Ana Flores
description: Proto-Symbolist painter. Sartan surname urban-born mixed heritage. Earth-toned palettes landscapes as witness. More abstract than Biku. Stayed in Guajicutea deepened visual vocabulary.

name: Andrés Guma
description: Proto-Symbolist theorist. Poet and essayist. Argued Guajicutean art should draw from own symbolic tradition not imitate Illpynian forms. Essays circulated in Sarta. Surname: guma (fire) plain root.

name: Fernando Paredes
description: PdA. Barirí successor. Steady unremarkable. Oversees tail end of depression. Sartan surname.

name: Pablo Yaya
description: PdA. Last PdA president. Rural base. Surname: yaya (earth/ground) plain root.

name: Francisco Navarro
description: PdI. First PdI president. Urban pro-trade. Sartan surname.

name: Miguel Karibá
description: PdI. Broadening beyond urban elite. Surname: kari (sea) + bá (place) = sea-place.

name: Salvador Ríos
description: PdI. War president. Led during War of Liberation (1853–1856). Sartan surname.

name: Rafael Aguilar
description: PdI. Post-war reconstruction. Guano boom begins. Sartan surname.

name: Ignacio Cruz
description: PdI. Faces workers riot (1861) PpE formation. Sartan surname.

name: Domingo Peña
description: PdI. Race riot (1866) immigration ban. Sartan surname.

name: José Moku
description: PdI. Signs public universal primary education (1870). Bridges to PpLT. Surname: moku (water) plain root.

name: Víctor Tabá
description: PdI. PdI-PpLT secret coalition era (1872). Surname: taba (stone) plain root.

name: Emilio Yabiku
description: PpLT. Coalition era PpLT dominates. Greater bureaucracy established (early 1880s). Surname: yabiku (wood-joining technique) plain root.

name: Hugo Garrido
description: PpLT. Licensing scheme established. Corruption scandals building during term. Sartan surname.

name: Arturo Medina
description: PdI. Gains ground as PpLT weakens from corruption scandals (~1888). Ironworks shuts down. Sartan surname.

name: César Bravo
description: PdI. Pre-war leadership. Catacombs rediscovered (1892). Sartan surname.

name: Roberto León
description: PdI. War president (Second War of the Isthmus 1893–1899). Slight majority. Income tax system established. Sartan surname.

name: Valentín Castro
description: PdI president PpLT Asamblea after 1899 flip (post-war recession). Ironworks purchased by Volisanian steel company. Sartan surname.

name: Lorenzo Mora
description: PpLT. Full power. Pushes left to compete with PdT. Ushers Constitutional Amendment of 1904 (women's enfranchisement). Sartan surname.
